title: One-paragraph impact tracker — Liam Ng
content:
Goal: ship measurable small-wins that move personal output & team velocity (one paragraph goal each week)

How I use this doc: quick weekly note (1 paragraph), 3 signal metrics, 1 experiment, 1 retrospective bullet. Replace every Monday. Keep it tiny.

Week of 2026-03-09 (current):
- One-paragraph goal: Reduce my average model endpoint iteration latency by 10% by adjusting batching config and pruning an unused transform step — aim to free 5–10ms p95 on dev tests so we can push config to canary.
- Signals (quantitative): median dev-run latency 48ms -> target 43ms; p95 82ms -> target 74ms; PR review cycle time 28h -> target 24h.
- Experiment: try smaller batch size + aggressive KV cache warmup on a 1000-request synthetic replay; measure token throughput and latency tail. Roll back if 2%+ regression in median. Tag PR: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2121 (draft).
- Retro (quick): yesterday I spent too long chasing flaky test; need to add a deterministic replay harness for this workload. Action: create ticket and pair with SRE this week.
- Notes to self: keep the paragraph to 1 sentence; if >2 sentences I'm overplanning. Save decision logs as a single-line in CONFLUENCE.

Open questions / friction:
- Do we prefer client-side batching changes or server autoscaler tweaks for short bursts? (ask @noah in sync).
- How to measure UX impact of 5–10ms savings for product clients — product metric mapping missing.

Micro-actions (this week):
- [ ] Run replay experiment (synthetic 1k req) and capture median/p95 by noon Thu.
- [ ] Open replay ticket and assign SRE (JIRA: ENG-8241).
- [ ] Draft 1-paragraph update for Friday team async (max 2 lines).
- [ ] If experiment succeeds, open canary config PR and add fallback policy.

Hypothesis log (for experiments):
- Hypothesis: removing transform X and warming KV cache reduces p95 without increasing median.
- Metric to watch: p95 latency (primary), median (rollback), token throughput (safety).
- Success criteria: p95 down >=8% and median down >=3% on dev replay.

Personal pulse: low friction day = focus finished tasks faster; aim for 3 small deliverables/week.

Backlog ideas (one-liners):
- tiny harness that replays sampled production prefixes to catch tail regressions.
- pair with product to define a client-visible latency SLO ladder.
- short doc: "When to prefer client batching vs server autoscale" (3 bullets).

Links / quick refs:
- replay harness draft: github.com/redwood-inference/replay-harness (wip)
- team okrs 2026: CONFLUENCE:TEAM-OKRS-2026
- notes from last retro: CONFLUENCE:RETRO-2026-02

Quick log (previous 3 weeks, 1-line each):
- 2026-02-16: focused on infra tidy; added dev-mode telemetry — freed 6ms median on local runs.
- 2026-02-23: experimented with quantization knob; cutoff reduced cost but increased p95 for long sequences.
- 2026-03-02: prototyped cache-warmup script; initial runs promising but not stable under concurrency.

End-of-week publish template (2 lines):
- TL;DR: small config change saved N ms p95 on dev replay; next: canary + product impact assessment.
- Ask: approve canary for limited traffic or hold for more synthetic runs.

Random scratch: "If I can make the decision in one line, ship it. If it requires a 15-min sync, schedule the 15-min sync."

TODO: prune this doc monthly (archive old weeks into a single monthly digest).
